Periods of weak scattered showers tonight will become isolated
tomorrow with the exception of minor island effect showers over part
of southern Guam. Isolated thunderstorms ahead of Bavi will begin as
soon as Saturday, becoming scattered Sunday. Shower chances will be
isolated Friday night into Saturday morning before increasing to
scattered Saturday afternoon as PWAT values increase ahead of Bavi.
Showers are expected to become numerous with locally heavy showers
possible Sunday, before becoming widespread heavy showers Sunday 
night into Monday. Strong, gusty winds Saturday night will likely 
reach tropical storm conditions Sunday and increase rapidly to 
Typhoon conditions late Sunday night or early Monday. Tropical storm 
conditions may return Monday night, dropping to windy by Tuesday.

Marine...
Combined seas of 3 to 4 feet and light to gentle trade winds are 
expected through Friday for the Marianas. The main swell is the east-
northeast trade wind swell. There will be a moderate risk of rip 
currents along east facing reefs of the Marianas through Friday 
night. Scattered showers are expected tonight. Saturday and Saturday 
night, a slight chance of thunderstorms will be possible before 
becoming a chance of thunderstorms Sunday through Monday night due to
the passage of current Tropical Storm Bavi, and then dropping back 
to isolated. Therefore, there will be a moderate risk of lightning 
Saturday then a high lightning risk Sunday and Monday. Shower chances
look to start increasing Saturday afternoon and by Sunday, Typhoon 
storm conditions are possible and lasting through Monday with winds 
as high as 140 knots near the center of Bavi according to the JTWC 
forecast. Seas and surf are expected to start building rapidly 
Saturday, July 4th as swell from Bavi approaches the Marianas. Seas 
and surf are expected to become hazardous as soon as Saturday 
afternoon. Seas of 25 to 35 feet are anticipated during the passage 
of Bavi Sunday and Monday with up to 40 ft seas possible near the 
center of Bavi. Tropical Storm conditions may subside by Tuesday 
night. This situation will continue to be monitored closely.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Storm Bavi (09W) is currently located to the north-
northeast of Pohnpei near 11.9N 158.5E, or roughly 930 miles east of 
Guam, 885 miles east-southeast of Saipan, and is moving west-
northwest at 15 mph. Satellite imagery this afternoon depicts a very 
broad, strengthening storm with deep convection becoming well-
consolidated around the center, focused along the western and 
northern flanks of the system. Heavy, deep showers extend roughly 200
miles west of the center, with newly developing heavy outer rain 
bands wrapping into the center from 250 miles out to the north, and 
from 300 miles out to the east-northeast. GLD network data shows 
occasional lightning within the flaring convection near the center, 
and within the distant convective bands to the east to east- 
northeast. Maximum sustained winds are 60 mph, and the latest 
forecast from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) shows TS Bavi 
strengthening to a typhoon within 24 hours, with maximum sustained 
winds increasing to 90 mph. 

Bavi is forecast to continue strengthening as it moves generally 
west-northwest toward the Marianas, potentially arriving to the 
islands as a strong Category 4 typhoon, potentially stronger, with 
maximum sustained winds forecasted to 155 mph. Model guidance 
continues to support an eventual track somewhere between Rota and 
Tinian, but certainty on the exact path remains low. Bavi could 
potentially pass anywhere from south of Guam to north of Anatahan in 
the northern CNMI, and there will be adjustments to the forecast 
track, and timing, in the coming days. Tropical Storm Bavi may arrive
to the Marianas sometime around late Sunday through Monday, but be 
prepared for changes in the expected time of arrival as Bavi speeds 
up, or slows down.

For more information on Tropical Storm Bavi, please refer to the 
Tropical Cyclone Public Advisory issued by the National Weather 
Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM and the Tropical Cyclone Warning
issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 
PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
Tropical Storm Bavi (09W) continues to slowly strengthen north of
Pohnpei. A southeast to south (inflow tail) wraps back towards 
Kosrae, so Some locally heavy showers are briefly possible there. 
Currently this looks to remain south of Pohnpei for the next 24 to 36
hours, but it'll eventually lift across Pohnpei as well. Then, as 
Bavi continues to strengthen and move slowly west-northwest, the 
"inflow tail" will broaden. Thus, at least scattered showers will 
stay in the forecast (locally higher coverage) through the start of 
next week.
